learning_outcomes.text: Select, write a technical report, and economically evaluate the electrical machines necessary for a specific industrial installation.
Perform, analyze, and write a technical report on the most common tests carried out on the electrical machines studied in the course.
Deduce and apply the equivalent circuit of the electrical machines studied in the course.
Calculate and analyze parameters and operating characteristics of the electrical machines studied in the course.
Calculate, design, and write technical reports for the electrical machines studied in the course.

syllabus_topics: Unit 2: General Aspects of Rotary Electrical Machines
Selection of asynchronous machines as generators
Selection of synchronous machines as generators

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory exam (physical execution of one lab practice)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, students can choose between continuous assessment (three partial exams and a lab exam) or a single final exam. For continuous assessment, a minimum of 30% is required in the theoretical part and 30% in each problem of each partial exam to be compensable, and an overall minimum of 5 out of 9 points for the partial to be approved. The final grade in continuous assessment is calculated as 30% for Partial Exam 1, 35% for Partial Exam 2, and 35% for Partial Exam 3, with a maximum contribution of 9 points from partial exams and 1 point from the lab exam, for a total of 10 points. If the minimum qualification is not obtained in each partial exam, the final grade will be a maximum of 4 out of 10. For the single exam, a minimum of 20% is required in each of its three blocks (corresponding to Units 1; 2 & 3; 4, 5 & 6). The final single exam grade is the sum of the weighted block scores: 30% for Block 1, 35% for Block 2, and 35% for Block 3. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required to pass the subject in the single exam option; if minimums are not met in each block, the maximum grade is 4 out of 10. Extraordinary call and differentiated evaluation follow similar rules to the single exam, with the same block structure, minimums, and weighting.
